findings.title: Spooled upload temp files are created world-readable (0644) on POSIX JVMs
findings.description: createTemp uses File.createTempFile, which on Unix opens the file with mode 0666 minus umask (verified: createTemp in java.io.tmpdir yields [OWNER_READ, OWNER_WRITE, GROUP_READ, OTHERS_READ]). With the default tempDirectory (java.io.tmpdir = /tmp on a JVM server) any other local account can read an in-flight or request-lifetime upload (documents, images, credentials uploaded by users) for as long as it is spooled, i.e. whenever a file part exceeds memoryThreshold (64 KiB default). Android is unaffected (app-private cache dir).
findings.suggested_fix: Right after File.createTempFile (file is still empty, so no exposure window for data) restrict it with java.io.File only: f.setReadable(false,false); f.setReadable(true,true); f.setWritable(false,false); f.setWritable(true,true). These are API 9 and java.io-only, so the Core constraint holds. Add a POSIX-only test asserting no group/other bits (the test may use java.nio in test code).

findings.title: Interrupt of a thread waiting in BodyState.sharedParse becomes a 400 and loses the interrupt flag
findings.description: A second thread calling req.form()/file() while another thread is parsing blocks in BodyState.sharedParse (BodyState.java:128 wait()). If it is interrupted (executor shutdownNow, app.shutdown force-close of in-flight work), InterruptedException is a checked Exception, so DefaultRequest.formData's generic catch (Exception) maps it to HttpException(400) and the thread's interrupt status is cleared; the interrupted worker sees a client error and no longer observes the interruption. Needs two threads sharing one request, so rare.
findings.suggested_fix: In sharedParse (or formData) catch InterruptedException, call Thread.currentThread().interrupt() and throw an HttpException(503) or IllegalStateException instead of a 400.

findings.title: Heap-growth test depends on System.gc() and whole-JVM heap readings
findings.description: FR_MULTIPART_004_AC2_spooledUploadKeepsHeapGrowthUnder8MiB compares MemoryMXBean used-heap before and after a 32 MiB in-memory upload with an 8 MiB tolerance. System.gc() is only a hint, and the figure includes the adapter's response buffers, other test threads and JIT/class loading, so a run under a different GC or a loaded CI box can exceed 8 MiB (false failure) while a regression that retained up to the tolerance would pass. The file itself is not in the P3 denominator, so this is reported from skimming.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert on the mechanism instead: a counting OutputStream/SpoolingBuffer test that the memory buffer never exceeds memoryThreshold bytes, or measure peak via a bounded -Xmx forked test.
